name: Aqua
explanation: Water is commonly used to dissolve or disperse other ingredients in a cosmetic formula.
note: Its presence alone does not indicate a product's overall performance.

name: Glycerin
explanation: Glycerin is a humectant used to help the skin retain moisture.
note: The effect depends on the full formulation and how the product is used.

name: Niacinamide
explanation: Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 used in skincare formulations.
note: Benefits depend on concentration, formulation, and individual skin response.

name: Hyaluronic Acid
explanation: Hyaluronic acid and its salts are used in products designed to help maintain skin hydration.
note: Different forms of this ingredient are not identical.

name: Panthenol
explanation: Panthenol is a form of provitamin B5 commonly used in skin and hair care products.
note: The benefit depends on the formulation.

name: Tocopherol
explanation: Tocopherol is a form of vitamin E that can help protect oils in a formulation against oxidation.
note: This does not establish the effectiveness of the finished product on skin.

name: Allantoin
explanation: Allantoin is used in some cosmetic products for skin conditioning.
note: Individual responses can vary.

name: Squalane
explanation: Squalane is an emollient used to help soften skin and reduce the feeling of dryness.
note: It is different from squalene.

name: Dimethicone
explanation: Dimethicone is a silicone ingredient used to improve slip and skin feel in cosmetic products.
note: Its role depends on the formulation.

name: Carbomer
explanation: Carbomers are used to thicken or gel certain cosmetic formulations.
note: This is mainly a formulation function.

name: Xanthan Gum
explanation: Xanthan gum is commonly used to thicken and stabilize products.
note: Its role varies by formulation.

name: Cetearyl Alcohol
explanation: Cetearyl alcohol is a fatty alcohol used to soften skin and help control product texture.
note: It is not the same as ethanol or rubbing alcohol.

name: Stearic Acid
purpose: Helps form and stabilize product texture
explanation: Stearic acid is a fatty acid used in some creams, cleansers, and other cosmetic formulations.
note: Its function depends on the formula.

name: Citric Acid
explanation: Citric acid is often used to adjust the pH of cosmetic formulations.
note: Its presence alone does not reveal the final product pH.

name: Phenoxyethanol
explanation: Phenoxyethanol is used as a preservative in many cosmetic products.
note: The finished product's compliance and safety depend on concentration and applicable regulations.

name: Ethylhexylglycerin
explanation: Ethylhexylglycerin is used in some cosmetic formulations as a skin-conditioning ingredient and preservative booster.
note: Its function depends on the formulation.

name: Sodium Hyaluronate
explanation: Sodium hyaluronate is a salt of hyaluronic acid used in skincare formulations.
note: It is related to, but not exactly the same ingredient name as, hyaluronic acid.

name: Zinc Oxide
purpose: May function as a UV filter or provide other formulation functions
explanation: Zinc oxide is used in cosmetics, including some sunscreens.
note: A label alone does not establish a product's sun-protection performance.

name: Titanium Dioxide
purpose: Colorant and, in some formulations, UV filter
explanation: Titanium dioxide is used as a pigment and in certain sunscreen formulations.
note: Its function depends on the product and formulation.

name: Parfum
explanation: Parfum is a label term for a fragrance ingredient mixture.
note: The word alone does not identify every component of the fragrance mixture.
